svg.data-weight-note: 20.5 kg (45.18 lb) with 2 PSUs and 4 fans installed - both documents agree
svg.data-air-filter: quick start guide, "Optional Air Filter": a filter behind a cover held by captive screws, attached and replaced in the field. An accessory rather than a fitted part, so it is recorded here and not modelled.
svg.data-humidity: Operating: 5% to 85% non-condensing; Storage: 5% to 95% non-condensing
svg.data-cpu: Intel Xeon D Ice Lake, 8-core 3.1 GHz
svg.data-switch-silicon: Broadcom BCM88851 Jericho2c+ with a BCM16000 OP2 TCAM
svg.data-software: ONIE preloaded; no NOS image ships on the device
svg.data-timing: 1PPS, 10 MHz and ToD ports, SyncE and IEEE 1588v2 PTP
svg.data-optics-sfp-plus: datasheet, power budget: "1.5 W on SFP+ ports". THE CAGES ARE SFP+ AND RUN 10G, which is what the panel legends them ("SFP+ 10G") and what the guide's lamp legend says ("LED1 (left) - Yellow (10G)"). No breakout or multi-rate table is published for this family and none is invented; what IS published is the combo restriction, below.
svg.data-optics-qsfp28: datasheet, power budget: "6.5 W on QSFP28 ports" - a 100G optic's envelope, not a 400G one. THE RATES ARE STATED BY THE LAMP LEGEND rather than by an optics table: "LED1 (left) - Blue (100G), Green (40G), Cyan (25G), Yellow (10G)", so the cage runs 100G, 40G, 25G and 10G. Whether 25G and 10G arrive by breakout or by a slower module is not said anywhere and is not guessed here.
svg.data-optics-qsfp-dd: datasheet, power budget: "23 W on QSFP-DD ports", which is a 400G ZR-class envelope. THE LAMP LEGEND AGAIN GIVES THE RATES: "LED1 (top) - Magenta (400G), Blue (100G), Cyan (25G), Yellow (10G)". The ordering text calls the cage QSFP56-DD - eight lanes of 50G PAM4 - while the panel legends it QSFP-DD 400G; the panel's wording is used.
svg.data-combo: quick start guide: the 10G SFP+ ports share a group with 100G QSFP28 ports 0 and 1; either the SFP+ ports or those QSFP28 ports can be used, and the two types cannot run at the same time.
svg.data-emissions: EN 55032, EN 61000-3-2, EN 61000-3-3, FCC Title 47 Part 15 Subpart B Class A

g.data-description: the four 10G SFP+ ports, a single ganged quad of two columns by two rows at the left of the face, numbered 0-3 down each column. THEY ARE HALF OF A COMBO PAIR: the guide says these ports share a group with 100G QSFP28 ports 0 and 1, and that either the SFP+ ports or those QSFP28 ports can be used but not both types at once, and the panel prints one continuous pink band across this quad and QSFP28 column 0 to say the same thing.
g.title: port-0

g.data-description: the twenty-four 100G QSFP28 ports, in three ganged blocks of two columns by four rows, the four rows falling into an upper and a lower bank with their own numbering bands above and below. Column k carries 4k and 4k+1 in the upper bank and 4k+2 and 4k+3 in the lower - a stride of four down each column - which is why this family is twelve two-port blocks in the layout rather than two twelve-port ones. PORTS 0 AND 1 ARE THE COMBO PAIR shared with the SFP+ quad.

g.data-description: the twelve 400G QSFP-DD ports, in three blocks of two columns by two rows. UNLIKE THE OTHER TWO FAMILIES THESE ARE NOT A BELLY-TO-BELLY STACK: each row is its own single-high ganged cage with its own bezel, and the panel's "QSFP-DD 400G" rule runs through the gap between them. Column k carries 2k and 2k+1. The datasheet's ordering text calls the cage QSFP56-DD; the panel says QSFP-DD 400G and the panel is followed.
